Your app broke at nine PM, and was fixed by ten. Here's how, in five DevOps steps.
Nine PM. Users report the pay button freezes. A developer finds the bug, writes a three line fix, and pushes it to GitHub. Git tracks every change, so nothing gets lost.
That push wakes up GitHub Actions, the robot of the pipeline. It builds the app, and packs it into a Docker container, so it runs the same on a laptop and on the server.
Three. Test. This step saves your weekend.
Hundreds of automatic tests run in minutes, even fake payments. If one test fails, the pipeline stops, and the bug never reaches your phone.
All tests pass. Kubernetes rolls out the new version slowly. Ten percent of users first, then everyone. Old servers keep running till the new ones are ready. Zero downtime.
Prometheus and Grafana watch the live app every second. If errors jump, an alert fires, and one command rolls back to the old version. Ten PM. Fixed.
Plan, code, build, test, deploy, monitor, on loop. That's DevOps. Save this, and send it to the friend learning cloud.
